criterion: At least one saved learner message. Participation does not establish proficiency.
description: Recorded participation in this language.
label: Experience

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for entities & reference.
label: Entities & reference

criterion: Identify a particular person or thing so the listener can tell which is intended.
description: Point out a person or an object you want to talk about.
label: Identify a referent

criterion: Keep multiple previously mentioned referents distinguishable across a connected statement.
description: Tell a story involving two friends and the different things they did.
label: Track several referents

criterion: Express a quantity or distinction between one and more than one with enough precision for the context.
description: Order food for a few people or describe what is in your bag.
label: Express quantity

criterion: Express a scope-sensitive quantity such as some, all, neither or only, with the intended set clear.
description: Talk about which friends like an activity and how many would join.
label: Qualify quantities

criterion: Make clear who something belongs to or its relevant part–whole relationship.
description: Talk about whose bag, keys, or bicycle you found.
label: Express possession

criterion: Identify a referent through multiple linked possession, part–whole or descriptive relationships.
description: Help someone find a particular object among several similar ones.
label: Specify a complex referent

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for properties & comparison.
label: Properties & comparison

criterion: Attribute a quality or state to the intended referent. Do not require an adjective word class or a copula.
description: Describe a person, a place, or an object you care about.
label: Attribute a property

criterion: Restrict a property by circumstance or perspective, making its intended scope clear.
description: Explain what you like about a place and what could be better.
label: Qualify a property

criterion: Express a clear comparison between identifiable referents along a stated or contextually clear dimension.
description: Choose between two places to visit or two things to buy.
label: Compare referents

criterion: Express a comparison with a precise standard, degree or exception.
description: Compare a new experience with something familiar.
label: Specify a comparison standard

criterion: Express the intensity or extent of a property in a way that fits the intended meaning.
description: Talk about how hot, busy, expensive, or enjoyable a place was.
label: Express degree

criterion: Express a degree in relation to a limit or consequence, such as too hot to drink.
description: Describe weather or a busy day that changed what you could do.
label: Connect degree to consequence

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for events & participants.
label: Events & participants

criterion: Express an event with the actor and other relevant participants distinguishable. Do not require a fixed word order or case system.
description: Tell someone about an activity you did with a friend.
label: Express who does what

criterion: Present an event from a non-default participant perspective while preserving who did what. Do not require a passive construction.
description: Discuss what happened to a lost item and who might have found it.
label: Change event perspective

criterion: Express a transfer with the thing transferred, source or giver, and recipient clear where relevant.
description: Describe giving a gift, lending a book, or sending a message.
label: Express transfer

criterion: Describe transfer with additional beneficiary, instrument or condition while keeping participant roles clear.
description: Plan how to get a package to a friend who will be away.
label: Express a constrained transfer

criterion: Express that a participant or event brings about another event or state.
description: Talk about something that made you change your plans.
label: Express causation

criterion: Distinguish causing, allowing or arranging an event from directly performing it.
description: Explain how a small event led to several changes in your day.
label: Distinguish causation and agency

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for time & event structure.
label: Time & event structure

criterion: Locate an event before the relevant present using target-language wording and context. Do not require tense inflection.
description: Tell someone about something you did yesterday.
label: Refer to past events

criterion: Make the relative order of multiple past events clear, including an event preceding another past reference point.
description: Tell the story of a trip from its start to its finish.
label: Order past events

criterion: Locate an event after the relevant present or reference point. Do not require a future-tense form.
description: Share something you would like to do this weekend.
label: Refer to future events

criterion: Distinguish a future intention, prediction or conditional event with the relevant timing clear.
description: Make a plan together and consider what to do if it rains.
label: Relate future possibilities

criterion: Distinguish ongoing, completed or habitual events where the distinction is supported by the current wording and context.
description: Discuss a habit you started, stopped, or want to keep.
label: Express event phase or repetition

criterion: Relate contrasting event phases or repetition patterns without confusing completion, duration or habituality.
description: Talk about what you were doing when something unexpected happened.
label: Contrast event structure

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for space & movement.
label: Space & movement

criterion: Locate an entity relative to an identifiable place or reference object.
description: Help someone find a café, a room, or an item in your home.
label: Locate an entity

criterion: Describe a spatial relation where the viewpoint or frame of reference matters and keep it clear.
description: Give directions from a station to a place you know.
label: Coordinate spatial frames

criterion: Express movement with relevant source, path or destination distinguishable.
description: Describe a walk or a journey through your neighborhood.
label: Describe movement

criterion: Describe a path with multiple spatial relations or changes of direction in a followable sequence.
description: Explain a route with several stops or changes of transport.
label: Describe a multi-stage path

criterion: Use context-appropriate here/there or proximal/distal reference with a recoverable intended location or referent.
description: Choose where to sit or which nearby object to pick up.
label: Use spatial reference

criterion: Maintain clear spatial reference when describing a different speaker’s or participant’s viewpoint.
description: Describe a place from your viewpoint and from a visitor’s viewpoint.
label: Shift spatial viewpoint

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for negation, questions & possibility.
label: Negation, questions & possibility

criterion: Express what does not hold with the intended event, property or participant scope clear.
description: Explain a preference or correct an assumption about your plans.
label: Negate a proposition

criterion: Distinguish materially different scopes of negation, such as not all versus none.
description: Clear up a misunderstanding about which people did something.
label: Control negation scope

criterion: Request confirmation or missing information with the intended question recoverable. Do not require inversion or a question particle.
description: Find out more about a partner’s hobby or daily routine.
label: Ask a question

criterion: Express an indirect or embedded question while keeping the requested information clear.
description: Ask someone to help you find out where or when an event happens.
label: Embed a question

criterion: Express ability, possibility, desire, permission or obligation with the intended force clear in context.
description: Discuss what you can do, need to do, or might do on a trip.
label: Express possibility or necessity

criterion: Distinguish a relevant difference in certainty, permission, obligation or ability rather than leaving the modal force ambiguous.
description: Plan an outing with choices, practical limits, and obligations.
label: Distinguish modal meanings

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Language strategies for connecting ideas.
label: Connecting ideas

criterion: Connect a proposition with a relevant reason or purpose so their relationship is clear.
description: Explain why you chose a hobby, a meal, or a place to live.
label: Connect a reason

criterion: Relate an outcome to a counterexpectation without confusing concession with cause.
description: Talk about enjoying something despite a difficulty.
label: Express concession

criterion: Express that an outcome depends on an identifiable condition.
description: Make an agreement about what to do if a situation changes.
label: Express a condition

criterion: Distinguish an imagined contrary-to-fact condition and its consequence from an actual event.
description: Imagine how a past trip would have changed with more time.
label: Express a counterfactual

criterion: Attribute speech, belief or thought to its source without confusing the source with the learner.
description: Share something a friend told you about their day.
label: Report speech or thought

criterion: Keep speaker, time and reference clear through an embedded or perspective-shifting report.
description: Discuss a story you heard through a friend and what each person believes.
label: Maintain perspective in reports

criterion: Progress summarizes direct evidence for the skills in this area; it does not imply all of them were demonstrated.
description: Practical language for social phrases.
label: Social phrases

criterion: Use an appropriate conventional thanks, apology, welcome or polite response.
description: Thank someone for a favor, apologize for a small mix-up, or respond to an offer.
label: Thank, apologize or respond politely

criterion: Ask or answer a conventional wellbeing check-in, such as how are you or I am well.
description: Ask how someone’s day is going and share how you are doing.
label: Exchange social pleasantries

criterion: Use a conventional greeting or farewell appropriate to the exchange.
description: Meet someone for the first time or end a friendly conversation.
label: Greet and say goodbye
